proposals.evidence: Turner explicitly records Oriya dādi, Hindi/Marathi dādā and Nepali dāi elder brother in the *dādda nursery kinship family. These single elder-brother responses match that documented family; dental/retroflex and repeated-nasal variants are preserved, and nursery diffusion rather than strict uniform sound-law descent remains possible.

proposals.evidence: Turner explicitly gives Kumaoni dādī grandmother/elder sister and neighbouring dād-/dadd- elderly-relative words under *dādda. Jaunsari and Nepal survey dadi/ḍāḍī/dāḍi fit this elder-sister use of the ā-vowel nursery family; the i-vowel didi family is separately treated under 6327.
